name: 3rd Sunday of Lent
description: The battle between God's kingdom and the power of evil.
biblicalBasis: Jesus drives out demons and is accused of doing so by Beelzebul (Luke 11:14-28, Matt 12:22-30). Jesus answers: "If it is by the finger of God that I drive out demons, then the kingdom of God has come upon you." The parable of the strong man who is bound by a stronger one. "Whoever is not with me is against me."
significance: God's kingdom breaks in as a confrontation with evil—not peaceful coexistence, but battle. Jesus reveals himself as the stronger one who binds Satan. There is no neutral option: "Whoever is not with me is against me." Lent is a time to choose sides and make room for God's kingdom.
liturgicalContext: Purple color. The theme of spiritual struggle deepens the character of fasting—it is not only about self-discipline, but about taking a stand in the battle between good and evil.
history: Exorcism and demonology were central themes in the early church's catechesis during Lent, as baptismal candidates were prepared to renounce the devil in baptism. This Sunday bears the mark of that pedagogy.
otConnections: God's finger who wrote the law on stone tablets (Exod 31:18)—the same finger of God now driving out demons. Elijah's battle against Baal's prophets on Carmel (1 Kings 18)—"How long will you limp between two opinions?" Daniel's struggle with the princes of darkness (Dan 10).

references.reason: The day is about the battle between God's kingdom and evil. The text about false prophets who are ravenous wolves, and the requirement to know them by their fruits, is directly relevant for distinguishing between God's kingdom and evil in a time of confrontation.

Matthew 8 is a central text for the 3rd Sunday of Lent. The chapter shows Jesus' power over sickness, death, nature, and demons, illustrating the battle between God's kingdom and the power of evil. Especially the driving out of demons (vv. 28-34) and the calming of the storm (vv. 23-27) emphasize that Jesus is Lord over all that threatens humanity, a central theme for Lent.

This passage (Matt 12:22-45) is the central text for the 3rd Sunday of Lent. It covers the entire narrative of the battle between God's kingdom and evil: the healing of the possessed man, the discussion about the strong man, the warning against blasphemy against the Spirit, the parable of the tree and its fruit (vv. 33-35), and the parable of the unclean spirit's return illustrating the condition of an evil generation. Extending the tag to verse 45 captures the full theological arc concerning the struggle against evil and judgment upon the evil generation.

The 3rd Sunday of Lent has the theme 'Bread from heaven' and the battle between God's kingdom and the power of evil. Jesus feeding the 4,000 (Matt 15:29-39) is a central text for this day, showing God's abundance and compassion toward the crowds.
